newsitem.title: USA: US West mega-bond deal raises credit risk concerns.
newsitem.headline: US West mega-bond deal raises credit risk concerns.

text.p: A collosal $3.5 billion debt offering by U.S. West Inc, has thrown a spotlight on new potential credit risks for bond investors in the fast-changing world of media and telecommunications.
"This is no longer your father's phone company," warned Carol Levenson, an analyst at Gimmie Credit Publications.
"US West's future is rife with uncertainty," she said, referring to the company's major investments in cable television. Cable is perceived as a much riskier industry than telecommunications.

The debt issue that the company's US West Capital subsidiary was preparing for Thursday would match the largest high-grade corporate bond issue in U.S. history -- last year's $3.5 billion issue by Lockheed Martin Corp.

Proceeds would be used to refinance debt related to US West's $11 billion acquisition of Continental Cablevision Inc last year. That acquisition triggered a three-notch downgrade of the company's credit rating, Levenson noted.
"Think of US West as a strong, stable, well-positioned local phone company with a far-less-profitable, debt-laden, capital-guzzling, competition-endangered cable business on its back," said Levenson.

One of the main concerns of bond investors is that US West may increase its ownership of Time Warner Inc's cable assets, triggering another potential downgrade. The company owns 25 percent of a Time Warner partnership that holds the assets.
According to analysts who have attended US West's recent roadshow, US West officials are doing their best to assuage investor fears.
"We would not do anything to impair our triple-B credit rating. We consider it a distinct strategic advantage, and intend to keep it that way," said a US West spokesman.

Investors are apparently buying the company's story. US West was able to increase the size of the current debt offering to $3.5 billion from an original $2 billion as a result of strong investor demand. Sources say the deal is still oversubscribed.

Dail St. Claire Simmons, a portfolio manager at New York-based money management firm, Utendahl Capital Managment, said, US West "is a highly leverged company, but you're being compensated for your risk. At this price, we are comfortable with the story."
Analysts note US West bonds are being priced at levels more typical of a cable company like News Corp or Time Warner, rather than long distance companies.
The bonds, which are rated Baa1/BBB-plus, are being issued by the funding arm of US West, and are guaranteed by the parent company. Price talk on the 10-year notes is 80-83 basis points.
Traders noted that the bonds of the US West Communications, the telecommunications subsidiary of US West have also widened since the company became so heavily involved in the cable industry.
"US West is now a hybrid cable operation that receives stong credit support from a communications subsidiary," said one trader.
